gdp_level.description: The total value of everything Hungary produces in a year, at current prices, on a rolling four-quarter basis.
gdp_level.dollar: “Dollarise” converts each historical point using that year's own average forint rate per US dollar (World Bank PA.NUS.FCRF, annual resolution, coarser than the monthly or daily matching on most other countries here, since no free monthly or daily US dollar series exists for the forint).
gdp_level.real: “Make it real” swaps this to Hungary's real (chained-volume, inflation-adjusted) GDP series (Eurostat namq_10_gdp, CLV20_MNAC). This strips out the effect of price changes, so it shows genuine output growth rather than growth that's really just inflation.
gdp_level.source: Eurostat namq_10_gdp (CP_MNAC) · current prices, forint, seasonally and calendar adjusted, quarterly, shown as a rolling four-quarter sum.

gdp_real.description: GDP adjusted for inflation, shown in chained-volume terms, the same production, valued at constant prices, so changes reflect real output growth rather than price changes.
gdp_real.dollar: Same matching as GDP (current prices): each point converted at its own year's average forint rate per US dollar (World Bank PA.NUS.FCRF).
gdp_real.real: This IS the “Make it real” series, toggling it off shows GDP at current (nominal) prices instead.
gdp_real.source: Eurostat namq_10_gdp (CLV20_MNAC) · chain-linked volumes, 2020 reference year, forint, seasonally and calendar adjusted, quarterly, shown as a rolling four-quarter sum.

gdp_growth.description: How much the economy grew or shrank compared with the previous three months, in real (inflation-adjusted) terms. The Hungarian Central Statistical Office's first estimate is often revised; this shows the latest published figure.
gdp_growth.dollar: A growth rate (%) is currency-agnostic, converting the underlying forint to dollars doesn't change the percentage change. “Dollarise” has no effect on this figure.
gdp_growth.real: This is already a real (inflation-adjusted) growth rate as published, “Make it real” has no additional effect on it.
gdp_growth.source: Derived from Eurostat namq_10_gdp (CLV20_MNAC) · real GDP, seasonally and calendar adjusted, quarter-on-quarter.

cpi.description: How much consumer prices are rising compared with a year ago, on the EU's harmonised index (HICP), shown for comparison with other EU countries. The Hungarian Central Statistical Office's headline is the national CPI, shown beside it, which the Magyar Nemzeti Bank targets at 3%. The two can differ by a few tenths because their weights differ.
cpi.source: FRED series CP0000HUM086NEST · HICP, all items, year on year.

cpi_mom.description: How much consumer prices changed in the month, on the EU's harmonised measure. A monthly change is not the annual rate divided by twelve: it is the change on the month before, so it moves with one-off price changes that the annual rate smooths out.
cpi_mom.source: Derived from FRED series CP0000HUM086NEST (Eurostat) · HICP, all items, change on the previous month, not seasonally adjusted.

cpi_national.description: How much consumer prices are rising compared with a year ago, on the Hungarian Central Statistical Office's national CPI, the headline figure and the measure the Magyar Nemzeti Bank targets at 3%.
cpi_national.source: OECD prices database · CPI, national definition, all items, year on year, computed from the OECD's copy of the Hungarian Central Statistical Office's index, from 2015. It can differ by 0.1 from the rate KSH publishes (September 2026: 1.54% here, 1.6% in KSH's release), because the index is rebased and rounded differently.

policy_rate.description: The base rate, the Magyar Nemzeti Bank's main policy rate. In 2022 and 2023 the MNB steered short-term rates with an 18% one-day deposit tender while the base rate stood at 13%, so market rates were higher than the base rate in that period. Shown from mid-2001, when the MNB adopted inflation targeting. The instrument behind the base rate has changed: the two-week deposit rate until January 2007, the two-week MNB bill until July 2014, the two-week deposit again until September 2015, and the three-month deposit rate since.
policy_rate.source: BIS central bank policy rates (WS_CBPOL, M.HU, extended with the daily series D.HU) · MNB base rate, end of month, from July 2001; the current month shows the latest rate.

bond_yield_10y.description: The yield on 10-year Hungarian government bonds, a market gauge of inflation and interest-rate expectations. This is not the MNB's own policy rate.
bond_yield_10y.source: ECB long-term interest rate for convergence purposes (IRS, M.HU.L.L40.CI.0000.HUF.N.Z) · 10-year government bond yield, monthly average, from 2001.

business_confidence.description: How optimistic firms are about the months ahead. 100 is the long-run average; readings above it mean firms expect better-than-average conditions.
business_confidence.dollar: This is an index, not a currency figure, “Dollarise” doesn't apply to it.
business_confidence.source: OECD · Business Confidence Indicator (BCICP), amplitude-adjusted, long-term average = 100.

unemployment.description: The share of people aged 15 to 74 in the labour force who want a job and are actively looking, but can't find one.
unemployment.source: Eurostat une_rt_m · unemployment rate, ILO definition, ages 15 to 74, seasonally adjusted, monthly.

participation_rate.description: The share of people aged 15-64 who are either working or actively looking for work.
participation_rate.source: FRED series LRAC64TTHUQ156S · OECD, ages 15-64, seasonally adjusted, quarterly.

employment_rate.description: The share of people aged 15-64 who are actually in work, regardless of whether others are looking.
employment_rate.source: FRED series LREM64TTHUQ156S · OECD, ages 15-64, seasonally adjusted, quarterly.

exports.description: The value of goods Hungary sells to the rest of the world each month, in forint.
exports.dollar: Each point is converted at its own year's average forint rate per US dollar (World Bank PA.NUS.FCRF), see the GDP entry for detail.
exports.source: Eurostat ext_st_27_2020msbec · exports of goods, world partner, monthly, converted from euros at each month's ECB reference rate (EXR M.HUF.EUR.SP00.A).

imports.description: The value of goods Hungary buys from the rest of the world each month, in forint.
imports.dollar: Each point is converted at its own year's average forint rate per US dollar (World Bank PA.NUS.FCRF), see the GDP entry for detail.
imports.source: Eurostat ext_st_27_2020msbec · imports of goods, world partner, monthly, converted from euros at each month's ECB reference rate (EXR M.HUF.EUR.SP00.A).

trade_balance.description: Exports minus imports of goods each month. Hungary usually sells more goods abroad than it buys; the balance turned negative in 2022, when energy import prices surged.
trade_balance.dollar: Each point is converted at its own year's average forint rate per US dollar (World Bank PA.NUS.FCRF), see the GDP entry for detail.
trade_balance.source: Eurostat ext_st_27_2020msbec · goods trade, world partner, exports minus imports, monthly, not seasonally adjusted, converted from euros at each month's ECB reference rate.

debt_gdp.description: Everything Hungary's central government, local government and social security funds owe combined, compared with the size of the economy.
debt_gdp.dollar: Already expressed as a % of GDP, currency-agnostic. “Dollarise” has no effect on this figure.
debt_gdp.source: Eurostat gov_10dd_edpt1 · EDP notification table, general government, % of GDP, annual.

deficit.description: The yearly gap between government spending and revenue across all levels of government, as a share of GDP. Negative means a deficit.
deficit.dollar: Already expressed as a % of GDP, currency-agnostic. “Dollarise” has no effect on this figure.
deficit.source: Eurostat gov_10dd_edpt1 · EDP notification table, general government, % of GDP, annual.

current_account.description: Hungary's overall balance with the rest of the world, trade in goods and services plus net investment income, as a share of GDP.
current_account.dollar: Already expressed as a % of GDP, currency-agnostic. “Dollarise” has no effect on this figure.
current_account.source: World Bank BN.CAB.XOKA.GD.ZS · % of GDP, annual.

fx_usd.description: How many US dollars HUF 1 buys. A rising number means a stronger Hungarian forint.
fx_usd.source: World Bank series PA.NUS.FCRF · official exchange rate, annual average, shown as US$ per HUF 1 (1 ÷ the published HUF per US$).

fx_eur.description: How many euros HUF 1 buys, on annual averages. A rising number means a stronger Hungarian forint.
fx_eur.source: Derived: World Bank PA.NUS.FCRF annual average (HUF per US$) and the annual average of Federal Reserve H.10 DEXUSEU; € per HUF 1 = (US$ per HUF 1) ÷ (US$ per €1).
